title: Overtime Grievance Under Conflicting CBA Terms
scenario_text:
Context from ADP (Payroll — Week ending Jun 15, 2026):
Employee: D. Wojcik (Badge 4412) | Classification: Maintenance Mechanic A | Shift: 2nd | Regular hours: 40 | OT hours: 12 | OT authorized by: T. Reeves (Shift Supervisor) | Cost center: Plant 2 Maintenance

**Microsoft Teams — #plant2-supervision (Jun 13, 2026, 9:52 PM)**
@tony.reeves: Need Danny W. to stay for a double. Compressor #3 is down and we can't run the heat treat line without it. @miguel.santos you around?
[No response — 45 minutes pass]
@tony.reeves: Going to call it — authorizing the OT. Can't wait, we'll miss the Pratt delivery window.
@rick.jensen: 👍
[rick.jensen is Union Steward, Plant 2]

**SharePoint — /HR/labor-relations/CBA-2026-final.pdf (effective Apr 1, 2026)**
Article 14.3: 'Overtime in excess of 8 hours beyond regular shift requires authorization from Plant Manager or designated Operations Manager. Shift Supervisor authorization is limited to first 8 hours of overtime only.'

**Shared Network Drive — \\plant2\ops\CBA-archive\CBA-2022-2025.pdf**
Article 14.3 (prior version): 'Overtime authorization rests with Shift Supervisor or above for all duration.'

**SAP PS — Production Order 4001910:**
Customer: Pratt & Whitney | Part: FORGE-9920-C | Due date: Jun 16, 2026 | Status: IN PROCESS | Constraint note: 'Heat treat cycle = 14hr minimum. Late start = missed ship date. LD clause active ($15K/day).'

**Email — Subject: 'CBA Rollout Training' (Mar 28, 2026)**
From: hr-laborrelations@ironforge-mfg.com
To: all-supervisors@ironforge-mfg.com
CC: plant-managers@ironforge-mfg.com

'Please review the attached summary of changes effective April 1. Key changes include updated OT authorization levels (Art. 14.3), new shift-swap procedures (Art. 16), and revised holiday premium calculations. Training sessions scheduled for April 5-9. Attendance is mandatory.'

**ADP — Training Records:**
T. Reeves: CBA Training — Status: NOT COMPLETED. Scheduled Apr 7, marked 'No Show.' No reschedule on file.

**Grievance Filing — Local 412, Case #2026-G-031 (filed Jun 20, 2026):**
Grievant: D. Wojcik | Nature: Improper OT authorization | Relief sought: Double-time pay for hours 9-12 of OT (penalty rate per Art. 14.5 for unauthorized OT) | Union position: 'Supervisor lacked authority under current CBA. Employee entitled to penalty premium.'

**Miguel Santos' Calendar — Jun 13, 2026:**
7:00 PM - 9:00 PM: 'Flight CLE→ORD' (personal calendar, blocked as OOO)
No delegation of authority memo on file for that date.
question: As Plant Operations Manager, how should Miguel assess the grievance merit and what is the most defensible resolution?

contributor.name: Miguel Santos
contributor.title: Plant Operations Manager
contributor.domain_expertise: Production scheduling, maintenance planning, labor relations, overtime authorization, collective bargaining agreement administration

choices: Grievance has no merit — the old CBA terms apply because Reeves was never trained on the new CBA, making enforcement of the new authorization levels against him improper

Grievance has merit — Reeves lacked authority for hours beyond 8 under the current CBA; however, the appropriate resolution is to pay the penalty premium for hours 9-12 only and issue corrective training to Reeves, not to discipline the employee
Grievance has merit and Ironforge should deny the OT pay entirely for hours 9-12 since it was unauthorized, paying only straight time
Grievance has no merit — the Union Steward's thumbs-up emoji in Teams constitutes implicit union consent to the authorization, waiving the procedural objection
